summary.name: Sitch
summary.one_liner: Sitch is a free, open-source, offline screenshot annotation app for Windows and Mac that revives the discontinued Skitch tool.
use_cases: annotate screenshots with arrows and text
redact secrets before sharing a screenshot
quick capture and paste into Slack or Mail
create step-by-step numbered instructions with screenshots
replace Skitch on Windows or Mac
summary.what_it_does: Sitch captures a screen region or window via a single hotkey (Ctrl+Alt+4 on Windows, or ⌘⌥4 on Mac) and opens it for annotation, with each capture placed on the clipboard. It offers 14 annotation tools including tapered arrows, text, shapes, highlighter, stamps with auto-numbered steps, spotlight, emoji, image overlay, and non-destructive crop, with undo and redo. The Obscure tool offers pixelate, blur, solid block, or stripes, flattened into the image on export. Export options include copy at full resolution, drag-and-drop, the macOS share sheet, and PNG, JPEG, PDF, or TIFF files. The page states it makes no network connections and has no account or telemetry.
notable: Open source under MIT license, with no account, subscription, or telemetry
Fully offline: the page states it makes no network connections
Native build: WPF on Windows, Swift and AppKit on Mac, not Electron
Redactions are flattened into pixels on export
caveats: Windows build is a portable .exe with no installer; the page says macOS 15+ is required
Page notes that blur and pixelation can sometimes be partially reversed, so solid block or stripes are recommended for real secrets
Price comparisons are stated as of 2026 and refer to competitors' pricing
